per_question.answer: If a container's liveness probe keeps failing, the kubelet kills the container and subjects it to its restart policy once the failure threshold is reached [1][2]. With a failing readiness probe, the container is not killed; instead the kubelet marks it as not ready and the Pod stops receiving traffic from matching Services, while continuing to run the container and its probes [1][2].

per_question.answer: When you create a NodePort Service without specifying a port, Kubernetes allocates a port from the range set by the `--service-node-port-range` flag, which defaults to 30000-32767 [1]. With the default range, automatic assignment uses the dynamic band (30086-32767) by default and may fall back to the static band (30000-30085) once the dynamic band is exhausted [3]. The static band is intended for users who want to pick specific ports manually, which lowers the risk of collisions [2][3].

per_question.answer: By default, a Pod's containers get 30 seconds to shut down gracefully after you delete it, since the default grace period is 30 seconds [2]. Kubelet begins local shutdown as soon as the Pod is marked terminating, and any `preStop` hook runs within that period [3]. If the `preStop` hook is still running when the grace period expires, the kubelet grants a one-off extension of 2 seconds [3].

per_question.answer: A brand-new Kubernetes cluster starts with four initial namespaces: default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, and kube-system [1]. The kube-node-lease namespace holds the Lease objects associated with each node, which allow the kubelet to send heartbeats so the control plane can detect node failure [1]. Each Node has a matching Lease object in kube-node-lease, and every kubelet heartbeat updates that Lease's spec.renewTime field, which the control plane uses to determine node availability [3].

per_question.answer: By default, `.spec.backoffLimit` is set to 6, so a Job retries failing Pods six times before it is considered failed [2]. Each pod failure counts toward this limit unless a pod failure policy is configured [1]. Failed Pods are recreated with an exponential back-off delay (10s, 20s, 40s, ...) capped at ten minutes [2].

The `Always` value is the one permitted for ReplicaSet templates, not Jobs [1].

per_question.answer: The kubelet first evicts `BestEffort` or `Burstable` Pods whose usage exceeds their requests, ordered by Priority and then by how far their usage exceeds the request [1]. `Guaranteed` and `Burstable` Pods whose usage is below requests are evicted last, based on Priority [1]. The QoS class is not what decides the order: the kubelet does not use it for eviction ordering, though it can be used to estimate the likely order [1][2][3].

per_question.answer: Anonymization means processing personal data so that, even when combined with other data, it can no longer be associated with an identified or identifiable natural person [2]. Under the law, personal data that is no longer needed for the reasons it was processed must be deleted, destroyed, or anonymized [1]. The procedures and principles for deletion, destruction, or anonymization are set out in a regulation [1].

per_question.answer: Kişisel verileri işleyen gerçek ve tüzel kişiler, veri işlemeye başlamadan önce Veri Sorumluları Siciline kaydolmak zorundadır [1]. Kurul, işlenen verinin niteliği, sayısı, veri işlemenin kanundan kaynaklanması veya üçüncü kişilere aktarılma durumu gibi objektif kriterlere göre bu kayıt zorunluluğuna istisna getirebilir [1]. Kayıt başvurusu, veri sorumlusunun kimlik ve adres bilgileri, işleme amacı, veri kategorileri, alıcılar, yurt dışı aktarımlar, güvenlik tedbirleri ve azami saklama süresini içeren bir bildirimle yapılır [1].

Bu yükümlülük, işlenmesini gerektiren sebeplerin ortadan kalkması hâlinde kişisel verilerin resen veya ilgili kişinin talebi üzerine veri sorumlusu tarafından silinmesi, yok edilmesi veya anonim hâle getirilmesi gerektiğini öngören Kanun'un 7. maddesine aykırılık hâline bağlıdır [1][2].

Aynı hüküm uyarınca üyeler resmî veya özel görev alamaz, dernek, vakıf ve benzeri yerlerde yöneticilik yapamaz, serbest meslek faaliyetinde bulunamaz, hakemlik ve bilirkişilik yapamaz [1]. Başkan, Kurul ve Kurumun başkanı sıfatıyla Kurumun en üst amiridir ve Kurum hizmetlerini mevzuata, amaç ve politikalara, stratejik plana, performans ölçütlerine ve hizmet kalite standartlarına uygun olarak düzenleyip yürütür ve hizmet birimleri arasında koordinasyonu sağlar [2]. per_question.answer: The aggregation layer proxies requests based on APIService objects: you register an APIService, which "claims" a URL path in the Kubernetes API, and from then on the aggregation layer forwards anything sent to that path to the registered APIService [1]. The most common way to implement that APIService is to run an extension API server in Pods within your cluster [1]. Until an APIService is registered, the aggregation layer does nothing for that extension resource [1].

per_question.answer: No. In apps/v1, a Deployment's `.spec.selector` is immutable after creation and cannot be updated via `kubectl patch`, `kubectl edit`, `kubectl apply`, or tools like `helm upgrade`; if it must change, the Deployment has to be deleted and recreated [1][2]. per_question.answer: A bare Pod (one with no owner reference) whose labels match a ReplicaSet's selector will be immediately acquired by that ReplicaSet [3]. Because the ReplicaSet is not limited to Pods created from its own template, it can take ownership of such Pods [2]. If the Pod is acquired after the ReplicaSet already has its desired number of replicas, the Pod is terminated, which is why bare Pods should avoid matching a ReplicaSet's selector [2].

per_question.answer: Use a DaemonSet when a copy of a Pod must always run on all or certain nodes, especially when it provides node-level functionality that other Pods need to run correctly on that node [1]. Deployments are generally recommended over managing ReplicaSets directly [3].

A PodGroup that references a non-existent (or deleting) Workload is rejected by the API server, while a Pod that references a not-yet-existing PodGroup stays pending until the PodGroup is created [2]. The Job controller is the only built-in controller that follows this pattern at present [1].

per_question.answer: To disable Memory QoS, set the `MemoryQoS` feature gate to `false`, ensure `memoryReservationPolicy` is unset or set to `None`, and restart the kubelet [1]. At startup, the kubelet resets `memory.min` and `memory.low` on the kubepods root cgroup and `memory.low` on the Burstable QoS cgroup to zero, and when disabled it sets `memory.high` to `max` for containers that are newly applied, restarted, or resized in place [1]. An already running container that is not restarted or resized may keep its previous `memory.high` value until its next restart or in-place resize [1].
